title: Characterization of frame preservation
statement: Let $C$ be a contract and let $F_{i,d,j}\subseteq\mathbb Z$ specify, for each datum $i$, starting configuration $d$, and tape $j$, a set of cell positions. The endpoint of every eligible run agrees with its starting configuration on every tape cell outside the corresponding set if and only if, for every such $i,d,j$ and every $q\notin F_{i,d,j}$, the endpoint's content at $q$ equals the starting configuration's content there.
hypotheses_covered: A set of integer positions is specified for each datum, starting configuration, and tape
replaced:
Let $C$ be a contract for a $k$-tape machine, and let $F$ assign to each parameter and
configuration a set of integer positions on each tape. The contract preserves every tape
cell outside these sets—meaning its endpoint agrees there with the starting
configuration for every entry-state configuration satisfying the precondition—if and
only if, for every such parameter, configuration, tape, and position outside the
assigned set, the endpoint tape content equals the starting tape content.
